title: The Barbero-Immirzi Field as a Hyperbolic Axion-Dilaton: Fixed Kinetic Mixing, the Spiral Twist Hypothesis, and a QCD-Anomaly Scale Test
description:
Version 3. This theory note separates the exact N=1 supergravity field-space geometry from the hypothesized Spiral Twist potentials and cosmological roles. The BI axion kinetic coupling remains fixed at lambda = -2 sqrt(2/3); the tests of the weak-mixing regime, solar-system constraints, and the constant-superpotential potential are retained with their limitations.

New in this version: an explicit QCD-anomaly scale assessment using the Nieh-Yan BI normalization F_phi = 2/sqrt(6 kappa) approximately 2.0e18 GeV and chi_QCD(0)^(1/4) = 75.6 MeV. The leading periodic approximation gives m_phi = sqrt(chi_QCD)/F_phi = 2.86e-12 eV, m_phi/H_eq = 1.14e16, and a radiation-dominated onset estimate T_osc approximately 46 MeV for 3 H = m_phi. It therefore describes an n=1 field that oscillates and redshifts as matter long before equality, not the separate n=3 equality-locked EDE ansatz or late-time quintessence.

The susceptibility is fixed at its zero-temperature value; relativistic degrees of freedom are held fixed; the equality-angle estimate uses a subdominant small-angle harmonic approximation and is not a Boltzmann likelihood fit. Thermal susceptibility, full BI-field normalization matching to the AEGIS arsinh map, and a full cosmological likelihood for this QCD candidate remain open.
